caption: A GameObject is a list of Components, each a C# wrapper over a native object: disabling one component stops only that component, SetActive(false) stops them all.
Every Transform write dirties the whole subtree below it, so two writes cost two propagations and SetPositionAndRotation costs one.
The fix to the prefab asset reaches every instance except Track 12, whose overridden m_Size wins.
Watch FixedUpdate run once, then zero times, then twice across three frames, while Update, LateUpdate and rendering run exactly once each.
Drawn to scale: elapsed time piles up and each 20 ms fixed step drains it, so 60 fps skips FixedUpdate on one frame in six and 30 fps runs it once or twice.
A coroutine is suspended at each yield return null and resumed by the engine after Update on the next frame.
At 3.2 KB per frame the garbage reaches about 1.7 MB in nine seconds and the collection blows the 16.7 ms budget; at zero GC Alloc both lines stay flat.
Destroy frees only the native side at end of frame; only Unity’s == operator notices, every plain C# null test still sees a live reference.
The serializer keeps public and [SerializeField] fields of supported types and silently skips everything else.
With the SRP Batcher, material constants stay on the GPU, so each draw uploads only its small per-object data.
Static batching, dynamic batching and instancing merge work into one draw; the SRP Batcher keeps separate draws but makes them cheap.
Each binary multi_compile keyword doubles the variant count: ten keywords fill all 1,024 squares.
